My old living-room HTPC is Atom-based and going on ten years old, so it was time for a replacement. That one has been moved to the basement, along with the XBone, and a new living-room HTPC was built around an i5, 16GB of RAM, a 950 series GPU, three SSDs in a RAID0 stripe, and all of that packed into a mini-ITX case.

My plan, indeed what I did, was to load Linux and have Kodi as my base UI, then use a launcher to get into Steam from there. I've loaded Kodi so many times on the various systems I have spread around that I can do it blindfolded, but I've never tried to get the two to play together. So, while I was waiting for my controller to ship, I got the Kodi interface tuned to my liking, got my OTA tuner working and talking with the front-end fine, got Netflix working, and finally got Steam Big Picture launching and playing nice.

Then my controller came in. Doesn't play well with Kodi at all when Kodi is launched natively. Apparently the thing relies pretty heavily on the Steam overlay to provide controller profile data to it. So I essentially had to take my entire GUI apart and approach it from the direction of having Big Picture as my front-end, and launching Kodi from there. Thankfully, there's a pretty good community profile for the Steam remote that works well with Kodi, because the default setup is completely worthless.

So now my setup is going into Big Picture automagically, and from there I can launch Kodi with just a couple of clicks, and I still have my TV and Netflix sources working fine. I'm still learning the ropes of the new controller, but so far I like it. My only real complaint is that I can't find a way to turn off the Kodi remote that doesn't leave the Steam overlay sitting on top of everything else -- and with the remote off, I can't close it. I have a Rii Mote (it's really not that great, but it's also only $16), that I can use to close it for now, but if anyone knows a fix, that would be way better.
To get the steam controller working outside of steam you need to set the udev rule.

To be clear, it was "working" and being identified properly, but something with the way Kodi grabs fullscreen control overrode its input. It would work fine to bounce a round in the menus, but the second I started up a video, it went dead, and I had to resort to the other remote.
